ca_planet_of_the_apes_wall.blurb: This top-rope wall sits inside Malibu Creek State Park in the Santa Monica Mountains, west of Los Angeles. All 17 routes are set up on a top rope, and the grades cluster between 5.10 and 5.12, with a single 5.9 and one 5.13 at the top end. The stone is the pocketed volcanic rock the park is known for. The face is shaded early and late in the day but can still feel warm when the sun is out. Weekends bring crowds, the lines at the left end tend to be rigged first, and parties often share ropes. Anchors sit well back from the lip, so extra anchor material helps keep the rope off the edge.
ca_planet_of_the_apes_wall.approach: From the main lot, follow the dirt road toward the visitor center, cross the creek and bear left. The wall comes up before the rock pool.

ca_abyss_boulder_the.blurb: A large seaside block at Promontory in Del Norte County, a short drive south of Crescent City, standing across a narrow corridor from the Main Wall. It carries 17 routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus five trad climbs. Grades sit mainly in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with one 5.13 and a few gentler lines around 5.8 and 5.9. The routes are short, roughly four or five bolts, but sustained. The rock is the steep, pocketed sandstone typical of Promontory, and the setting is salty and exposed to the coast. It suits experienced climbers after hard, powerful single pitches.

ca_the_amphitheater_2.blurb: The Amphitheater is a section of The Mill, a basalt crag on a canyon rim at the edge of the Ishi Wilderness in northeast California. It holds 17 routes, nearly all sport with two trad lines, running from 5.8 up to 5.12. The largest group sits at 5.11, with a decent handful of 5.10s and 5.12s, so it suits strong intermediates and up rather than beginners. Routes are single pitch and well regarded for quality. Shade here is patchy and has varied since a fire thinned the cover. From the top of the approach trail, go left past the Great Roof area and this is the next section.

ca_boy_scout_wall.blurb: Boy Scout Wall is a sunny dome of clean, featured, high-angle slab in Bowman Valley, a granite sport-climbing zone in the Sierra off the I-80 corridor in the Tahoe region. Of its 17 routes, 15 are bolted sport lines and two are top ropes. Grades center on 5.10, which accounts for about half of the routes, followed by a handful of 5.11s, two 5.12s and a couple of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. That spread suits a solid 5.10 climber looking for a day of laps. The slab angle means technical footwork rather than steep pulling.
